children: Hallador Energy shares rose after the company said it closed a $600 million senior secured term loan facility to help pay for its proposed natural gas project.
The stock advanced 8% to $15.90 Thursday. Shares are still down 15% this year.

The power producer plans to use the borrowings to fund the construction of its proposed 460-megawatt natural gas-fired Turtle Creek Gas project. The money will also go toward upcoming payment obligations under Hallador's turbine asset purchase deal, as well as transportation and refurbishment costs.

The loan facility should represent the largest component to Hallador's overall financing plan for Turtle Creek, the company said. Management believes Hallador has a credible pathway and sufficient time to fully fund the project consistent with its objective.

The loan consists of $550 million funded at closing and an additional $50 million delayed draw term loan commitment available for up to 12 months. It has a three-year term and, subject to lender approval, a two-year extension option.

In connection with the facility, Hallador also has the ability to establish a super-priority revolving credit facility of up to $75 million with a similar tenor, creating a financing package of up to $675 million.

The Turtle Creek project is expected to cost less than $800 million. About $120 million of the proceeds from the loan facility will be used to repay Hallador's existing $45 million term loan and $75 million revolving credit facility.

Hallador said Thursday that development on the project continues to progress, despite certain milestones having taken longer than initially anticipated. The company still has the same view on Turtle Creek's economics and its targeted commercial operation date.

Turbine shipment is on schedule, and Hallador intends to complete the purchase of the equipment in line with its previous deal. Negotiations on the project's engineering and construction agreement are in their final stages.
